audioOverviews.title: تقديم صوتي للوحة انطباع، شروق الشمس

texts.historicalContext: Monet painted the outer harbour of Le Havre from a hotel window in the early morning. Exhibited in 1874, the picture helped give the Impressionist movement its name.
texts.artisticAnalysis: Boats, cranes, masts and chimneys dissolve into blue-grey mist. The small orange sun and its broken reflection create the strongest colour contrast and organise the whole scene.
texts.palette: Thin, rapid strokes preserve changing light rather than describing every object. Orange and blue-grey act as complementary colours, making the sun appear unusually intense.
texts.culturalSignificance: The painting became a defining statement of modern vision: an image of atmosphere, industry and a fleeting moment rather than a polished academic narrative.
interestingFacts: It depicts the port of Le Havre at dawn.
Its title inspired the name Impressionism after the 1874 exhibition.
